subject: Cardinal Health — private cluster throughput cascade & mitigation request
messages:
From: Jason Li <jason.li@cardinalhealth.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Cardinal Health private cluster — p95 spike + 502s

Hi Mateo,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and intermittent 502s across our Cardinal Health VPC private deployment starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate climbed from 0.2% to ~3.8% and throughput dropped ~30% on the main inference route (/v1/generate). This is impacting order validation flows — downstream backlog building up.

Attached is a small sampling of traces and a subset of service logs (svc-logs-partial.tar.gz). We can keep the cluster on the current config if you prefer, but throughput keeps dropping. Can your team triage? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether any config toggles (kernel fallback, smaller batch) we can flip without a deploy.

Thanks,
Jason
Senior SRE, Cardinal Health
Ops pager: +1-555-0199

Attachments: trace_dump_2027-07-08.json (6MB), svc-logs-partial.tar.gz (45MB)

From: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Jason Li <jason.li@cardinalhealth.com>, ops@cardinalhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 09:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health private cluster — p95 spike + 502s

Jason — thanks for the data. I've started an initial investigation with SRE and runtime. Early signals: a KV cache eviction storm on the shard serving the main route across nodes that correlates with high tail latency, and a small percentage of inference requests falling back to the slower attention kernel (seen in traces).

Immediate asks we've put in motion:
- Dumping full KV-cache telemetry for the shard (Vivek)
- Switching the deployment to the conservative kernel selection on a canary subset (non-disruptive toggle) for 10% of traffic (Laura)
- Temporarily lowering max_batch_tokens to reduce queuing (Mateo)

I can schedule a 20-min triage with our runtime engineers in 30 if that helps. Will upload a mitigation runbook once we confirm safe toggles.

Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
(Available: 09:45–17:00 PDT)

From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health private cluster — p95 spike + 502s

I've spun up the conservative-kernel canary (10% traffic) on the affected pool and watching. Initial telemetry (first 12 minutes) shows p95 on canary down ~20% vs baseline; 502s ceased for that slice. Will continue to monitor for 1 hour before proposing wider rollout.

Notes from triage:
- KV cache eviction rate spiked when several long-lived sequences hit identical prefix keys; seems workload mix changed (more long prompts).
- Some nodes reported GC pressure at the OS level coincidentally; we'll correlate with infra metrics.

Action items:
1) Mateo to confirm with Cardinal whether we can perform a staged rollback to conservative kernel across all pools if canary stabilizes.
2) Vivek to collect full KV telemetry and a list of affected shard IDs and node IDs.
3) Marissa to prepare a short mitigation runbook for Cardinal with exact toggles + rollback steps.

- Laura (Runtime PM)

Attachment: mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf (draft)

From: Jason Li <jason.li@cardinalhealth.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops@cardinalhealth.com, Priya Shah <priya@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health private cluster — p95 spike + 502s

Thanks team — good to see canary improvement. Priya: we can approve a conservative-kernel rollout if Redwood provides a succinct rollback plan and a short post-mortem note. Two asks from our side before full roll:
1) Can you confirm any functional deltas (model outputs) when kernel switches? We have a tight QA window.
2) We'll want the change scheduled outside our peak (not before 19:00 PDT).

Please include expected impact on token cost and any cache-warmup behavior we should expect.

—Jason

From: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Jason Li <jason.li@cardinalhealth.com>, ops@cardinalhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health private cluster — p95 spike + 502s

Jason / Priya — quick update after the evening validation window. Canary at 10% held stable overnight; p95 reduced and 502s are back to baseline. We ran functional diffs on 350 canonical prompts: no meaningful output regressions (differences within expected stochastic variance). Token cost on conservative kernel is +3–5% per token on our benchmarks, but throughput SLOs return.

Plan for next steps (proposed tonight, post-19:00 PDT):
- Ramp conservative kernel from 10% -> 60% over 30 minutes, monitor p95 and 5xx.
- Lower max_batch_tokens across pool to 1024 for 2 hours to reduce queuing windows; revert if no benefit.
- Activate targeted KV-preservation hints for long-lived sessions (best-effort, non-disruptive).

We will not change model weights or quantization. Marissa attached the mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf with exact toggles and rollback commands; Vivek has uploaded KV telemetry to the shared drive link. If you approve, we will proceed at 19:15 PDT.

Mateo
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-555-0142

Attachments: mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf
Related links: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c/cardinal-ops

Subject: Approval: Proceed with staged kernel ramp and batch reduction

Thanks — we approve the staged plan at 19:15 PDT. Two remaining asks for the record:
1) Please confirm an exec summary note within 2 business hours after the ramp completes (include p95, 5xx, and cost delta).
2) Add a short prioritized backlog item to investigate why long-lived sequences suddenly increased; we need root cause for our change control.

We'll hold off on any wide deploys until we see the post-ramp exec note.

Priya Shah
VP, Platform Engineering — Cardinal Health
priyaa.shah@cardinalhealth.com
